title: AMD Launches Helios Rack AI System as Microsoft Becomes Its Newest Major Cloud Buyer
excerpt: Microsoft will deploy AMD's Helios platform to power new Azure AI inference VMs, marking AMD's most significant challenge yet to Nvidia's dominance in data center AI infrastructure.
body:
• Microsoft announced three new Azure VM families powered by AMD's latest silicon, including the ND MI455X v7 built on AMD's Helios rack-scale platform
  • Helios delivers up to 2.9 exaFLOPS of FP4 AI performance per rack using 72 Instinct MI455X GPUs, directly challenging Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72
  • Azure HDv2 VMs will feature nearly 500 AMD EPYC CPU cores and 4TB of RAM, designed for AI data preparation and agent coordination at scale
  • The announcement comes ahead of AMD's Advancing AI 2026 keynote on July 23, where CEO Lisa Su is expected to detail production timelines

Three New Azure Offerings

Microsoft on Monday unveiled a sweeping expansion of its Azure AI and high-performance computing infrastructure built on AMD's most advanced silicon. The company announced three upcoming Azure virtual machine families: HDv2 for AI data processing, HXv2 for electronic design automation, and ND MI455X v7 for large-scale AI inference — the last of which is powered by AMD's Helios rack-scale platform.

"AI workloads are scaling faster than any single infrastructure approach can support," Microsoft said in a blog post by executive vice president Scott Guthrie. "We continue to evolve Azure's infrastructure, including expanding its AI fleet with AMD's most advanced AI and high-performance computing solutions."

https://x.com/UttamMarketJ/status/2079190893441974316

Helios Takes Aim at Nvidia

The ND MI455X v7 virtual machines represent the most strategically significant of the three announcements. Built on AMD's Helios architecture, they bring rack-scale AI inference to Azure for the first time using AMD accelerators — a direct challenge to Nvidia's dominance in cloud AI infrastructure.

The Helios platform packs 72 AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs into a single rack alongside next-generation EPYC "Venice" CPUs and Pensando Vulcano network interface cards. It delivers up to 2.9 exaFLOPS of FP4 performance per rack with 31TB of HBM4 memory, connected through an open Ethernet-based fabric using the Ultra Accelerator Link over Ethernet standard.

That open approach is AMD's primary differentiator. While Nvidia's competing NVL72 system relies on proprietary NVLink technology, Helios is built on the Open Compute Project's Open Rack Wide standard, allowing customers to avoid vendor lock-in.

"Engineering teams are pushing the limits of simulation, chip design and scientific computing. At AMD, we experience those demands firsthand as we design future AMD EPYC CPUs and AMD Instinct GPUs."

— Mark Papermaster, Executive Vice President and CTO, AMD

Purpose-Built for AI Data Pipelines

The HDv2 virtual machines address a less glamorous but equally critical bottleneck in AI infrastructure: the CPU compute that feeds data to GPU accelerators. Featuring nearly 500 6th Gen AMD EPYC CPU cores, 4TB of RAM, 32TB of local NVMe storage, and 400 Gb Azure Boost networking, the VMs are designed for data preparation, search, reinforcement learning, and agent coordination at scale.

The HXv2 VMs, meanwhile, target semiconductor design firms with 176 EPYC cores clocked above 5 GHz, 50% more cache per core, and 800 Gb InfiniBand — a nod to the growing intersection of AI and chip design. AMD itself is a major user of the existing HX-series VMs for designing its own processors.

The Competitive Landscape

Microsoft's investment in AMD's Helios underscores a broader industry trend toward heterogeneous AI infrastructure. While Nvidia remains the dominant force — its Vera Rubin platform is already shipping to eight cloud partners — hyperscalers are actively diversifying their GPU supply chains. Microsoft also deploys its own custom silicon alongside AMD and Nvidia hardware.

AMD's Advancing AI 2026 keynote, scheduled for July 22-23 in San Francisco, is expected to provide production timelines and additional customer announcements. Cantor Fitzgerald recently raised its AMD price target to $700, the highest on Wall Street, citing the company's momentum in AI compute.

For the tens of thousands of Indian-origin engineers working in cloud infrastructure, AI systems, and semiconductor design at companies like Microsoft, AMD, and their partners, the Helios rollout represents both new technical capabilities and growing career opportunities in a market expected to exceed $200 billion in annual infrastructure spending by 2028.
